thesisQuality.note: Record revenue/backlog and expanding launch plus space-systems scope support a strong integrated-space thesis, tempered by execution intensity.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Q2 revenue rose 62% YoY to a record $234M and backlog rose 137% YoY to $2.36B.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: About $40.59B market cap and ~52.85x sales against a still loss-making business embed substantial expectations.

catalystScore.note: 90+ launch backlog, Neutron development, and more than $1B of new Q3 contracts cited by management create multiple execution catalysts.

governancePower.note: Founder-led execution has expanded contracts and vertical scope, while aggressive acquisition/capital strategy warrants a governance discount.

alignment2036.note: Launch, spacecraft, communications and defense infrastructure directly align with expanding orbital infrastructure needs.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Launch services, space systems and planned communications ownership create explicit vertical integration across the stack.

bottleneckControl.note: Integrated launch plus spacecraft capability controls multiple scarce execution steps, though larger launch and satellite competitors remain.

scenarioRobustness.note: Commercial, civil and national-security demand diversify end markets, but Neutron and acquisition execution create scenario sensitivity.

substitutionResilience.note: Flight heritage, backlog and vertical integration increase switching friction, but launch and spacecraft alternatives remain credible.

supplyChainResilience.note: Vertical integration improves control of critical subsystems, while aerospace supply chains and development programs remain capital- and component-intensive.

pricingPower.note: Rapid backlog growth and contract wins support value capture, but current evidence does not establish monopoly pricing power.

risk1.note: Primary risks are extreme valuation, continuing losses, 15.68% YoY share-count growth, Neutron execution and integration/capital requirements.

confidence.note: Current issuer operating evidence and independent current market data support all numeric components; customer-level backlog concentration remains a non-gating unknown.

thesis: Rocket Lab is evolving from launch provider into an integrated space infrastructure platform spanning launch, spacecraft and communications, with rapid revenue and backlog growth.
keyRisk: The market valuation discounts substantial future success while losses, dilution, Neutron execution and acquisition integration remain material.
nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 revenue/backlog conversion and Neutron/Iridium execution milestones.
